notes:
Snapshot from AE/SE touchpoints — lots of shorthand below. Customer = mid-market B2B SaaS (helpdesk automation + customer success workflows). Primary goal: replace incumbent LLM API after repeated latency regressions impacting streaming UX. Interested in Hosted first for speed to value; Dedicated to follow for predictable throughput and cost when POC scales.

POC scope: chat agent with tool calling (calendar lookup, ticket lookup, CRM read) + streaming responses to product UI. Want time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for stream and p95 end-to-end for short-chat flows (<200 tokens). Also measuring token cost and per-session concurrency.

Benchmark notes (internal POC runs):
- Incumbent (baseline): streaming TTFB median ~120ms, p95 spikes to 800-1200ms under realistic concurrency (30 concurrent UI sessions). Frequent mid-response stalls observed.
- Redwood Hosted (initial tests): streaming TTFB median ~90ms, p95 ~180-220ms depending on model/config (impressive). Under same concurrency (30 sessions) p95 ~210ms with continuous batching enabled; very few stalls.
- Observed behavioral diffs: Redwood stream chunks arrived more consistently; fewer partial reconnections. Tool calling happened inline without long pauses.

Customer quotes from demo: "We had users abort the chat because the spinner froze — that's the main pain." "If Redwood can guarantee streaming SLOs we can move to production."

SE notes from Ethan: used adv. batching + prefix KV cache for repeated context in support flows; suggested quantization profile (int8) for Dedicated proofing to reduce cost. Suggested route policy: host primary (Redwood Hosted) + fallback to cheaper model variant for degraded throughput.

Security/Compliance: needs SSO/SAML, audit logging for API calls, KMS integration for key control, and ability to keep EU customer data in EU region for residency. Legal asked for DPA + SOC2 docs (provided link).

Commercial: Budget conversation ongoing — finance wants committed pricing for Dedicated (monthly) vs metered for Hosted. AE shared draft pricing (drive link). Forecast midpoint depends on Dedicated sizing after POC.

Shortcomings/unknowns: final SLA thresholds legal will sign off on; hops to Dedicated and migration runbook; network egress cost estimate for high-volume streaming; few function-call edge-cases to validate (multi-tool choreography).

Bottom line: strong migration intent driven by reliability/latency. Hosted API wins on immediate latency/stability in POC; Dedicated desired for predictable costs and capacity once we sign contract.
